title: The two response operations of a notice are in no source inventory
source: Legacy RWB-E4-036 endpoints; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.15; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1
section: 4 Flow; 12.1 REST operations provided; 16 Test cases
description: The legacy story names only the two notice operations that the module copies, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices with Litigation C and GET /notices/{noticeId} with Litigation R, and the module specification gives the customer self-service answer no operation at all. TSD P6 T-A.1 stops at API-P6-011 and holds no operation for a response of a notice, so the paths, the request and answer shapes, the statuses and the idempotency rule of the two operations this capability needs are not given by any source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-036 Endpoints table rows POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId}; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 with no response operation; FSD P6 v3 A2.15.2 steps 1 to 3 describe the answer but name no operation
proposed: Declare POST and GET /notices/{noticeId}/responses under /api/recovery/comms/v1 in RWB-P6-E4036-CON with an Idempotency-Key on the POST and the statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, and build them in RWB-P6-E4036-APP.

title: No source declares the row that holds the response of the customer to a notice
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and T3.0; Legacy RWB-E4-036 data table
section: 11 Data; 12.7 Tables owned
description: TSD P6 T3.1 defines notice, template, merge_field and signature_request for this module and no response table, and the legacy data table of RWB-E4-036 names notice, recovery_case, v_ace_customer, treatment, decision_log_entry and rule_row only. The field names, the physical types, the required flags and the DF field ids of the response row are therefore not given by any source, and the acceptance cannot be stored without a decision on them.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 object list (notice, template, merge_field, signature_request); Legacy RWB-E4-036 Data table rows recovery_case, v_ace_customer, treatment, notice, decision_log_entry and rule_row
proposed: Declare notice_response in rwb_comms with id, notice_id, case_id, response_code, channel, responded_at, decision_record_id and the standard columns of TSD P6 T3.0, fix the names, the types and the required flags in RWB-P6-E4036-CON, and create the table from RWB-P6-E4036-APP with the index on notice_id.

title: The capability area and the right of a customer-facing answer are not given
source: Legacy RWB-E4-036 permission checks; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1
section: 10 Authority; 12.1 REST operations provided
description: The legacy permission check of RWB-E4-036 names Litigation C and Litigation R, which is the module template copy for the two notice operations, and TSD P6 T6.1 holds no customer role and no right for a self-service answer: its rows are staff and system roles with the Documents, Litigation and Case record letters. No source states the capability area, the right or the scope that governs the response operations, and none states how the customer is identified at the edge.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-036 Permission checks table rows Litigation C and Litigation R; TSD P6 v2 T6.1 rows 1 to 44 with no customer role
proposed: Declare the capability area Litigation with right C on the POST and right R on the GET, scope applied, on the two response operations, enforce them at gateway-bff, and keep the role lists as rwb-access data.

title: The three consumed shapes and the two consumed events have no contract story on this key
source: Ownership Map v1; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 42; WP B-P6-02 C row
section: 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The response needs the offer of the case from S2 rwb-treatment, the record of the acceptance on the case from P3 rwb-case, the contact point and the consent of the party from P1 rwb-source-data (DP-05), and the events TreatmentApproved and CaseStateChanged. The plan names no contract story of those owners in this key contract dependencies and no source gives the path or the shape of the case acceptance record or of the source-data contact point read, so all of them are consumed and faked.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 rows GET /treatments/{treatmentId} owner S2, recovery_case owner P3, contact_point_ext owner P1; Architecture v5 slide 42 rows 05 and 10 with rwb-comms as a consumer; WP B-P6-02 story line with an empty C list
proposed: Declare the three shapes and the two events as consumed and faked in RWB-P6-E4036-CON, carry their paths as placeholders, derive the fakes from the owners published documents and add the C rows when the owner contract stories are planned.

title: The decision code, the response-code list and the source of the rule version are not given
source: Legacy RWB-E4-036 AC1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16 and R-RES-17; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2
section: 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.3 Events published; 14 Validation and messages
description: Legacy AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, and the routing table names the events CUSTOMER_SIGNED for an accepted and signed offer and CUSTOMER_DECLINED for a declined offer. No source names the decision code of a response, the list of response codes and its values, or the table that holds the rule version in force, so the decision element can name only the rule id and its reference data.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-036 AC1 line the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16 and R-RES-17 event columns; TSD P6 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-NOTICE and others with no response list
proposed: Carry the decision code, the response-code list and the rule version as reference data read with the version in force, name the rule ids R-RES-16 and R-RES-17 in the decision element, and keep every value as the placeholder until the reference data is published.

title: The response surface and the refusals beyond the two module messages are not given
source: FSD P6 Communications v3 Screens and A2.15; Legacy RWB-E4-036 screen and validation table; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2
section: 5 Exception paths; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: The only P6 screen of the FSD is SCR-33 Template approval, which shows a template and its states, and no source names a self-service or officer surface for a response, so the surface and its identifier are open. The messages beyond MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 are not given either: no source states the text or the message ID of a notice outside the eligible states, of a notice already answered, of an expired offer or of a legal hold, and no source states whether one notice may carry a second distinct response or which LOV-CHANNEL code represents the HOME.SCB channel.
evidence: FSD P6 v3 Screens table with SCR-33 only; Legacy RWB-E4-036 Screen and states table and Validation and messages table; TSD P6 v2 T3.2 LOV-CHANNEL values with no HOME.SCB value
proposed: Serve the two operations and no screen of this service, reach the surface through the gateway-bff composite route, keep one response per notice, and carry the refusal texts and the channel mapping as placeholders until the message list and the reference data are published.

title: RWB-P6-E4038: no dispute operation, request, answer or table exists in the P6 sources
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 TSD P6 Communications v2 (T3.1, T-A.1); Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 (A2.17.3.2)
section: TSD P6 T3.1 Object and field definitions; TSD P6 T-A.1 Endpoint inventory; FSD P6 A2.17.3.2 Field catalog
description: FEAT-COM-04 asks for the outcome only. The endpoint inventory of the module holds API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 and none is a dispute operation, T3.1 holds notice, template, merge_field and signature_request and no dispute table, and the field catalogue of the feature lists notice fields only. The two operations under /api/recovery/comms/v1, the DisputeRequest and Dispute shapes, the new notice_dispute table of rwb_comms, its element names, physical types, required flags and state list, and the row's DF field ids are therefore fixed by RWB-P6-E4038-CON and marked wherever no source names them.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P6-001 to API-P6-011; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 headings notice, template, merge_field, signature_request; FSD P6 v3 A2.17.3.2 is a notice field list; Architecture v5 slide 17 OUT names schema rwb_comms with notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery only
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-comms at the contract baseline review
proposed: Publish the two operations, the two schemas and the notice_dispute row in RWB-P6-E4038-CON on Day 1 with the placeholders of section 11, and take the missing element definitions to the data steward before the wave 3 readiness review.

title: RWB-P6-E4038: no published rwb-deviation operation raises X1 for a customer dispute, and TSD P6 T5.2 does not list S8
source: Ownership Map v1 (rows POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} owned by S8); Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.2
section: Ownership Map api rows owned by S8; TSD P6 T5.2 Cross-module interfaces
description: R-UNI-04 gives the X1 raise, its code, its owner and the pause of the case to the deviation owner, and the Ownership Map gives the deviation paths to S8 rwb-deviation, but no S8 contract story is planned for this key and T5.2 names P3, P4, P5, P6 and P7 only. The call, its request and answer elements and the deviation reference of the dispute are therefore consumed and faked, no contract dependency row is declared, and the unanswered-raise branch (202 with no reference, the stop kept, a retry and an alert) is this run's decision.
evidence: Ownership Map rows POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} owned by S8; TSD P6 v2 T5.2 names P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 and not S8; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives S8 the X1-X7 screening, pause, handling and return; no S8 CON story is named in RWB-P6-E4038-APP or RWB-P6-E4038-CON
owner_role: Owner of rwb-deviation and the Tech lead of rwb-comms
proposed: Declare the deviation create as consumed and faked with no C row, and add the C row RWB-S8-...-CON when an S8 contract story is planned; until then the fake and the 202 branch carry the risk.

title: RWB-P6-E4038: the rights matrix has no customer row, so a self-service dispute has no declared principal
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.17.3.3; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 20
section: TSD P6 T6.1 RBAC matrix; FSD P6 A2.17.3.3 Roles and permissions; Architecture v5 slides 13 and 20
description: The FSD names the Customer (borrower) as the primary actor of FEAT-COM-04 and the Complaint officer as the also-user, but T6.1 lists staff, partner and system principals only and holds no customer row. The principal of the two dispute operations, its token, the case scope it carries and the coarse permission at the edge are therefore not given by any source; the story declares the capability area and the rights on the operation and names the customer principal as gateway-bff's.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T6.1 rows run from RW-CASEOWN to SY-AGENT with no Customer row; FSD P6 v3 A2.17.3.3 names Customer (borrower) as primary; Architecture v5 slide 20 gives sign-in, the coarse permission and the composite route to gateway-bff and rwb-access
area: Access and edge, rwb-comms (P6) with gateway-bff and rwb-access (P4)
owner_role: Platform route owner and the security architect
proposed: Declare the customer principal as the edge's and add the row to the rights matrix and the access contract at the wave 3 readiness review, without writing a role code in the story.

title: RWB-E4-038: the legacy screen, permission and endpoint rows describe notice administration, not a customer dispute, and TSD P6 T8 maps its requirement to another feature
source: 04 User stories Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E4-038; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T8; Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 requirements served
section: Legacy Screen and states, Permission checks and Endpoints tables; TSD P6 T8 Requirement traceability; FSD P6 requirements served
description: The legacy story body is a customer self-service dispute, but its screen is SCR-33 Template approval, its permission table names Litigation C and Litigation R for two notice administration operations, and its endpoint block names the notice create and the notice read. TSD P6 T8 maps REQ-OCC-011, which is the customer self-service requirement the feature serves, to FEAT-COM-01 and not to FEAT-COM-04. The rows are therefore carried as belonging to the notice and template features and not copied into the dispute stories.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-038 Screen and states row SCR-33; Permission checks rows Litigation C and Litigation R; Endpoints rows POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId}; TSD P6 v2 T8 row REQ-OCC-011 mapped to FEAT-COM-01; FSD P6 v3 feature table row FEAT-COM-04 with requirement REQ-OCC-011
area: Story content and requirement traceability, rwb-comms (P6)
owner_role: Business analyst, P6, at the story review
proposed: Keep the legacy rows with RWB-P6-E1052-APP and the template stories, and correct the T8 mapping to FEAT-COM-04 in the next TSD version; no Litigation right is claimed for the dispute operations.

title: RWB-P6-E4038: the contact stop and its lift are named by two events whose payload, key and local projection are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 IN line and slide 42 event rows 06 and 07; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-05 and R-UNI-44
section: Architecture v5 slide 17 rwb-comms IN; slide 42 rows 06 and 07; TSD P6 T3.1 notice
description: Slide 17 gives rwb-comms the events DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared with the words contact stop, and slide 42 gives their owner, topic and consumers, but no source gives their payload, their key, the stop state they set or the way the stop is projected on the notice. TSD P6 T3.1 holds hold_reason (DF-LEG-032, varchar(30)) and no stop state, so the carrier, the projection and the state list of the dispute row are this run's decision and the event element is declared as the consumer's only.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 17 IN: events DeviationRaised / Cleared (contact stop); slide 42 rows 06 DeviationRaised and 07 DeviationCleared with topic rwb.deviation.events.v1 and consumers rwb-case, rwb-comms and rwb-treatment; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 notice row DF-LEG-032 hold_reason varchar(30); R-LIT-05 and R-UNI-44 name the hold and the resume but give no state name
area: Event consumption and data model, rwb-comms (P6) and rwb-deviation (S8)
owner_role: Owner of rwb-deviation with the Tech lead of rwb-comms
proposed: Fix the consumer element of the two events and the hold_reason carrier in RWB-P6-E4038-CON, and ask the S8 owner for the published payload and key before the app story is done.

title: RWB-P6-E4038: no source gives the dispute reason codes, the dispute state list, the decision code, the rule id or the refusal texts
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.17.3.1 and A2.17.3.2; 04 User stories Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E4-038
section: FSD P6 A2.17.3.1 Validation rules and BR-P6-017; legacy Validation and messages table
description: BR-P6-017 forbids writing in code a value a business person may change, and the feature gives the validation rules and six messages that belong to contact and dispatch, but no reason-code list, no dispute state list, no decision code, no rule id and no refusal text or message id for the two dispute operations. The values are therefore reference data, parameters and message-list entries read with the version in force, and the refusals carry the placeholder of section 14.
evidence: FSD P6 v3 A2.17.3.1 gives VR-P6-017-1, VR-P6-017-2 and BR-P6-017 only; legacy RWB-E4-038 Validation and messages gives MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-P6-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003; no source lists a dispute reason code or a dispute state
area: Reference data and message list, rwb-comms (P6)
owner_role: Configuration owner and the owner of the message list
proposed: Publish the reason-code list, the dispute state list, the decision code, the rule id and the refusal texts as reference data and message-list rows before the wave 3 readiness review; the stories read them and never write them.

title: contact_point_ext and the consent state are P1 extension tables while the legacy story and the FSD hold them as P6 data
source: Legacy RWB-E4-039 data table; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.2; Recovery Workbench Ownership Map v1 (contact_point_ext, party_ext)
description: The legacy story lists contact_point_ext (DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026) and v_ace_contact (DF-ACE-075 to DF-ACE-083) in the data table of a P6 Communications feature, and the FSD describes the consent, verification and failed count as held in recovery.contact_point_ext. The Ownership Map gives contact_point_ext, party_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext to P1 rwb-source-data in rwb_source_data, on the basis of Architecture v5 slide 41 (P1 owns the extension tables), the FSD P1 v3 change note and TSD P1 v3 T3.1, and gives the thirty v_ace_* views to P1 as its ACE view contract. The two readings cannot both hold for one owner.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-039 data table row contact_point_ext with DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026; FSD P6 v3 A2.18.2 consent, verification and failed count are held in recovery.contact_point_ext, keyed by the composite contact key; Ownership Map contact_point_ext owner P1
proposed: Read and write the contact point and its consent state only on the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05); declare no contact table, no consent column and no v_ace_* query in rwb_comms, and record the move in the Change Register.

title: No source names a published operation of the rwb-source-data contract for the contact read or the consent write
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 41; Recovery Workbench Ownership Map v1 (api rows owned by P1)
description: This story consumes two operations of P1 rwb-source-data: the read of a party's contact points with their consent state, and the write of one contact point's consent and verification state. Architecture v5 slide 15 names only GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}, GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId=, GET /freshness and POST /business-days/{date}/ready for that service, and the Ownership Map holds no contact or consent operation of P1. The paths and the element lists of the two consumed rows are therefore unknown, and the plan names no P1 contract story that could publish them.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 15 rwb-source-data IN rows (customers, accounts, collateral, payments, freshness, business day ready); Ownership Map api rows owned by P1 (customer and data-product rows only, no contact operation)
proposed: Build the two rows as consumed and faked on the rwb-source-data contract with the path and the element list as placeholders; add the C row and the pinned path when P1 publishes the operations in a contract story.

title: No operation and no screen of the contact repository exist in the P6 sources
source: Legacy RWB-E4-039 endpoints and screen tables; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 and T3.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18
description: The legacy endpoints of RWB-E4-039 are POST /cases/{caseId}/notices (Litigation C) and GET /notices/{noticeId} (Litigation R), which are the notice operations API-P6-001 and API-P6-002 of TSD P6 T-A.1 and belong to the notice stories. TSD P6 T-A.1 holds eleven operations (API-P6-001 to API-P6-011) and none is a contact operation, and T3.1 holds notice, template, merge_field and signature_request and no contact table. The legacy screen is SCR-33 Template approval, which shows a template and its approval states, and no source of the module names a contact repository screen.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-039 endpoints POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}; TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P6-001 to API-P6-011; legacy screen row SCR-33 Template approval
proposed: Declare the two contact operations as new on /api/recovery/comms/v1 in RWB-P6-E4039-CON, leave the two legacy notice operations to the notice stories, and serve the surface through the gateway-bff composite route without naming a screen identifier.

title: The consent state set, the verification rule and the failed-count threshold are not given by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E4-039 data table; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.2 and A2.18.3.1; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2
description: The legacy row names consent_given, consent_at, verified_at and failed_count as fields of contact_point_ext with DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026, but no source gives the value set of the consent state, the rule that makes a contact point verified, the threshold at which the failed count matters, or the rule id and rule version the decision log entry must carry for a consent change. TSD P6 T3.2 holds no consent list, and BR-P6-018 of the FSD only states that such values are read from reference data with their version.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-039 data row contact_point_ext (consent_given, consent_at, verified_at, failed_count) DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026; FSD P6 v3 A2.18.3.1 BR-P6-018; TSD P6 v2 T3.2 lists without a consent list
proposed: Carry the consent set, the verification rule, the failed-count threshold and the decision code as parameters and reference data read with the version in force, with the placeholder in the contract, and let the compliance and PDPA officer confirm the values before the baseline review closes.

title: The legacy Litigation C and R rights cannot serve the primary role of the feature
source: Legacy RWB-E4-039 permission checks; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.3.3
description: The legacy story copies the permission checks of the notice operations, Litigation right C and Litigation right R, and lists the roles that hold them. TSD P6 T6.1 gives the compliance and PDPA officer, the primary actor of FEAT-COM-05, Documents RU and Litigation R only, so that role holds neither Litigation C nor a Litigation update right and could not maintain a contact repository under the legacy right.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-039 permission checks Litigation C (RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE) and Litigation R (RW-CASEOWN and others); TSD P6 v2 T6.1 row RW-COMPLY Compliance and PDPA officer with Documents RU and Litigation R
proposed: Declare the contact read as Documents right R and the consent write as Documents right U with scope applied, keep the legacy Litigation rights on the notice operations that the notice stories build, and confirm the two rights at the baseline review.

title: The composite contact key, the eight unnamed contact_point_ext fields and the local stop projection are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E4-039 data table; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17
description: The FSD states that the consent state is keyed by the composite contact key, and the legacy row gives contact_key and contact_type plus eight fields it leaves unnamed, but no source defines the composite key, the eight fields or their physical types, and none defines the shape of the local projection in which rwb-comms keeps the contact stop of the two consumed deviation events. Architecture v5 slide 17 names only the two events.
evidence: FSD P6 v3 A2.18.2 keyed by the composite contact key; legacy RWB-E4-039 data row contact_point_ext with 8 more fields, DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026; Arch v5 slide 17 IN DeviationRaised / Cleared (contact stop)
proposed: Fix the composite key, the unnamed fields and the physical types as placeholders in RWB-P6-E4039-CON, and build the stop projection as the service's own P6 row keyed by the case reference the events carry, with no contact value and no consent state.

title: The registration of a payment intent and the contact read of this capability are in no source and have no contract story
source: Ownership Map v1 (api rows of P8, table rows of P1); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 rwb-payment IN and OUT and slide 41; TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.2
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The legacy key pays against the plan or the settlement but names no operation for the act, and neither the Ownership Map nor any source of this run names an operation that registers a payment intent against a plan or a settlement: the P8 rows of the map are GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match, and Architecture v5 gives rwb-payment GET /cases/{id}/payments and POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate inside its own service. The consent state per channel and the contact stop that VR-P6-016-1 and VR-P6-016-2 need are P1 facts behind the rwb-source-data contract, whose operation is not named for this key either. No P8 and no P1 contract story is named in the Contract dependencies of these two stories, so both rows are declared as consumed and faked and no C dependency is added.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 api keys GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match (owner P8) and table keys proceeds, treatment, contact_point_ext; Architecture v5 slide 17 rwb-payment IN REST GET /cases/{id}/payments and POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate; FSD P6 A2.16.2 integration points HOME.SCB, payments; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 dependency classes
owner_role: Solution architect with the owner of rwb-payment
proposed: Consume the payment-intent registration of the rwb-payment contract and the consent and contact-stop read of the rwb-source-data contract, declare both as consumed and faked rows with a one-hop 2 s budget, and add the C rows when P8 and P1 publish their contract stories.

title: No source names an operation or a screen for FEAT-COM-03: the endpoint inventory stops at API-P6-011 and the legacy story copies the two notice operations
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T8; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.16 and requirements served; Legacy RWB-E4-037 Endpoints and Screen and states
section: 2 Business rationale; 4 Flow; 12.1 REST operations provided; 15 Screens and states; 18 Traceability
description: The endpoint inventory of the module holds eleven operations, API-P6-001 to API-P6-011, and none of them is a self-service payment, and the requirement traceability routes REQ-OCC-011 to FEAT-COM-01 and gives FEAT-COM-03 no row of its own. The legacy story copies the two notice operations of the module, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices with Litigation C and GET /notices/{noticeId} with Litigation R, which are the operations of RWB-P6-E1052-APP and not the act the story describes, and its screen block names SCR-33 Template approval, which shows a template and its approval states and cannot show a payment. The self-service screen is the customer screen on HOME.SCB and the web that FSD P6 A2.16.2 names as an integration point, and no source gives its identifier, its field list or its route.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 with no self-service payment operation; TSD P6 v2 T8 row REQ-OCC-011 to FEAT-COM-01; legacy RWB-E4-037 Endpoints rows POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} and Screen and states row SCR-33 Template approval; FSD P6 v3 A2.16.2 integration points HOME.SCB, payments
proposed: Declare POST and GET /notices/{noticeId}/payment-intents under /api/recovery/comms/v1 in RWB-P6-E4037-CON with the Idempotency-Key on the POST and the statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, build them in RWB-P6-E4037-APP, and record the self-service screen as the HOME.SCB customer screen with its identifier left to the channel stories.

title: No source declares the row or the element set that holds a self-service payment intent
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.0, T3.1 and T3.3; Legacy RWB-E4-037 Data table; Ownership Map v1 tables
section: 11 Data; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan
description: TSD P6 T3.1 defines notice, template, merge_field and signature_request for this module and no payment-intent entity, the notice row of T3.1 carries no payment field across DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034, and the legacy data table of RWB-E4-037 names treatment, notice, decision_log_entry, rule_row, template and v_ace_customer only, so the intent, its owner reference and its owner state have no entity of their own in any source. The element names, the physical types and widths, the required flags, the DF field ids and the indexes of the row are therefore not given, and the acceptance cannot be stored or answered without a decision on them. The row is declared as payment_intent in rwb_comms and every unnamed part carries the placeholder.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 object list (notice, template, merge_field, signature_request); TSD P6 v2 T3.3 relationship list with no intent; legacy RWB-E4-037 Data table rows v_ace_customer, treatment, notice, decision_log_entry, rule_row and template; Ownership Map v1 table keys notice, template and merge_field (P6) with no payment_intent key
proposed: Declare payment_intent in rwb_comms with the intent id, case_id, notice_id, target, channel, the owner reference, the owner state, requested_at and the standard columns of TSD P6 T3.0, fix the names, the types and the required flags in RWB-P6-E4037-CON with the DF field ids as the placeholder, and create the table with ix_payment_intent_notice_id and ix_payment_intent_case_id in RWB-P6-E4037-APP.

title: No source gives the value sets of a self-service payment: the eligible notice states, the targets, the owner state, the decision code and the rule id
source: FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.16.3.1 and A2.16.3.2; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-RES-09 and R-SET-04
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: BR-P6-016 requires every value a business person may change to be read from reference data with its version, and no source gives the lists: A2.16.3.1 holds VR-P6-016-1, VR-P6-016-2 and BR-P6-016 only, and the list of values of T3.2 holds LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE, LOV-LANG, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-SIGN-METHOD, LOV-SIGN-STATUS and LOV-SIGNATURE-BASIS with no target list and no instruction-state list. R-RES-09 and R-SET-04 place the offer with the customer and name no payment amount, target, channel, fee or cut-off. The decision code and the rule id of the act are named by no source either, and the notice states in which a payment is accepted are not given.
evidence: FSD P6 v3 A2.16.3.1 rows VR-P6-016-1, VR-P6-016-2 and BR-P6-016; FSD P6 v3 A2.16.3.2 field catalog with no payment field; TSD P6 v2 T3.2 nine lists and no target or state list; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-09 and R-SET-04
proposed: Hold the eligible notice states and the target list as parameters of rwb-comms, read the channels and the owner state set as reference data with the version in force, and take the decision code and the rule id from the reference data of rwb-decision; set every value at the baseline review and never in code.

title: The role matrix of the module names no capability area and no right for a customer-facing self-service payment
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T6.2; Legacy RWB-E4-037 Permission checks; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.16.3.3
section: 10 Authority; 12.1 REST operations provided
description: The matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 holds two capability areas only, Documents and Litigation, with 44 staff, partner and system roles, and names no customer-facing right, while the legacy permission checks of RWB-E4-037 carry the Litigation C and Litigation R rows of the two notice operations the story copied, which are not the act the story describes. The primary role of FEAT-COM-03 is the customer (borrower), whose sign-in, case scope and masking at the edge are ACE Common, gateway-bff and rwb-access concerns. The capability area and the right of the two new operations are therefore a decision of the contract baseline, recorded as such, with the value and the role lists left to rwb-access.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T6.1 two capability areas and 44 roles with no customer role; legacy RWB-E4-037 Permission checks rows Capability area Litigation, Right C with RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE, Right R with a long role list; FSD P6 v3 A2.16.3.3 row Customer (borrower) Primary
proposed: Declare one capability area with right C on the POST and right R on the GET in RWB-P6-E4037-CON, keep the role lists in rwb-access, and confirm the customer path with the gateway-bff and ACE Common owners before the baseline is tagged.

title: No source names the event that reports a completed payment and no source gives the refusal messages of a payment intent
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 A2 event catalogue; TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.3; Legacy RWB-E4-037 Validation and messages
section: 12.3 Events published; 12.4 Events consumed; 14 Validation and messages
description: The catalogue of Architecture v5 slide 42 holds PaymentMissed, TreatmentBooked and ProceedsMatched from rwb-payment and no event that reports a completed payment, and TSD P6 T5.3 names three published notice events only, so the event that would close a reference as paid is not given and the paid state is read from the owner answer. The legacy validation table holds six messages, of which MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 are reused here, and it gives no message ID, no text and no status for a notice outside the eligible states, for an owner that answers that there is nothing to pay against, or for an owner that does not answer.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 rows 05, 08, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15 with no completed-payment event; TSD P6 v2 T5.3 three published events; legacy RWB-E4-037 Validation and messages table six rows; FSD P6 v3 A2.16.4.3 rows AC-EXC-P6-016-01 and AC-EXC-P6-016-02
owner_role: Business analyst with the owner of the message list
proposed: Read the paid state from the owner answer until rwb-payment publishes a completed-payment event in the catalogue, and take the message IDs, the texts and the statuses of the three unnamed refusals from the owner of the message list; carry them as the placeholder until then.

title: No operation in the P6 endpoint inventory serves an offer view on a digital channel
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14; legacy RWB-E4-035 endpoint block
section: 12.1 REST operations provided; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story declares only the two notice operations of the module, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices (API-P6-001) and GET /notices/{noticeId} (API-P6-002), and the endpoint inventory of TSD P6 holds eleven operations from API-P6-001 to API-P6-011, none of which shows an offer to a customer on a channel or records a customer view. FSD P6 A2.14 describes the feature as a customer action on a screen and names the integration points LINE OA and HOME.SCB but no operation. The two operations of this key, the channel-view read and the view record, are therefore new and appear in no inventory.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 rows API-P6-001 to API-P6-011; legacy RWB-E4-035 Endpoints table with the two notice paths; FSD P6 v3 A2.14.2 integration points
owner_role: P6 service owner and solution architect
proposed: Build the two operations as declared in RWB-P6-E4035-CON, GET /notices/{noticeId}/channel-view and POST /notices/{noticeId}/views on base /api/recovery/comms/v1, marked new, and add both rows to the API Specification and the endpoint inventory at the next version.

title: The offer and the customer, contact point and consent are other services facts with no contract story to depend on
source: Ownership Map v1 (treatment owned by S2, party_ext and contact_point_ext by P1); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.2; legacy RWB-E4-035 data table; Template and Rules v1 R5.4
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes
description: The legacy feature reads v_ace_customer (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074) and treatment (DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-014) as rows of the same schema as the notice. In the target the offer and its validity are S2 rwb-treatment and the customer, the verified contact point and the consent are P1 rwb-source-data, and the plan names no P1 and no S2 contract story in the C list of this key. The two reads are therefore declared as consumed and faked, and the data product code of the contact point, the offer field names and the key of TreatmentApproved stand as placeholders.
evidence: Ownership Map tables treatment (owner S2), party_ext and contact_point_ext (owner P1); legacy RWB-E4-035 Data table rows v_ace_customer and treatment; WP B-P6-02 story line with C []
proposed: Consume GET /data-products/{productCode}/records of rwb-source-data and GET /treatments/{treatmentId} of rwb-treatment one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, faked from the first run; add the C rows when the two contract stories are planned, and name the data product code and the offer fields when the owners publish them.

title: No source states which event a digital view raises, and the proof-of-delivery element has two possible paths
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 rows 13 to 15; TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.3; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.1 metric; RWB-P6-E1055-CON and RWB-P6-E2021-APP
section: 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 12.3 Events published
description: The catalogue gives rwb-comms three events, NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered, and states neither the trigger of the third nor whether a customer view of an offer on LINE or on the portal raises it. The WIN proof-of-delivery stories already publish NoticeDelivered from the returned letter, so a digital view would be a second writer of the same event on the same topic, and no source states the rule that keeps one delivery event per notice across the two paths.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 row 15 NoticeDelivered with consumers rwb-litigation, rwb-guarantee and rwb-case; TSD P6 v2 T5.3 lists NoticeDelivered as published with no trigger; RWB P6 E1055 APP and E2021 APP publish it for the WIN path
owner_role: P6 service owner and event owner
proposed: Publish rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1 on the first delivery of a notice, WIN or digital, reusing the element RWB-P6-E1055-CON declares and adding channel additively; a later view records the view and publishes nothing. State the once-per-notice rule in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog when it is next versioned.

title: No field of the notice carries the channel of a digital delivery or the fact of a view
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.2; legacy RWB-E4-035 data table
section: 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan
description: The notice row of TSD P6 T3.1 carries id, case_id, document_id, notice_type, sent_date, barcode, callback_date, delivery_status, sent_type, party_id, template_id, hold_reason, dispatch_file_id and dispatch_attempts, and no field carries the channel of a digital delivery or the identifier of a view. title: No source declares the right of an offer view, a customer role, or a web channel value distinct from PORTAL
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1 and T6.2 and T-A.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.3; legacy RWB-E4-035 permission checks
section: 3 Preconditions; 10 Authority; 12.1 REST operations provided
description: The matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 holds staff, partner and system roles and no customer role, and no letter of Documents or Litigation is named for an offer view. The legacy permission check gives the two notice operations Litigation C to RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE and Litigation R to a long list. The feature is used by the customer (borrower) on LINE OA and HOME.SCB, so the identity that calls the two operations on behalf of the customer is not stated anywhere, and LOV-CHANNEL holds PORTAL with no WEB value, which leaves the mapping of the web channel open.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T6.1 rows RW-CASEOWN to SY-AGENT with no customer row; TSD P6 v2 T3.2 LOV-CHANNEL from MOBILE to BRANCH with no WEB; legacy RWB-E4-035 Permission checks table

proposed: Declare the two operations with the capability area and the right of the notice resource they extend, Litigation R on the read and Litigation C on the write, and leave the customer identity to the gateway-bff route; map the web channel to PORTAL and add a customer role or a channel service identity to rwb-access at the next version.
